mcp_connectors.description: Connectors are per-user connections to organization-defined external services. Each connector stores the user's credentials and exposes the remote service's tools for use through chat. Users refer to these as "connectors" in the UI.

agents.description:
Agent is an AI-powered assistant that users can interact with, configure, and delegate/schedule tasks to.

An agent is composed of two linked records:
- agents — identity: name, title, avatar, custom_role (permissions), and a manager (the only user that can manage/update the agent)
- agent_configs — behavior: the system instructions the agent uses

Each agent_config belongs to exactly one agent via its `agent` relationship.

Both records must exist for an agent to have behavior. The agent_config is created as a separate record referencing the agent; the `agent_config` field on the agents record is populated automatically from that link.

An agent acts like a regular user:
- it has a permission set (custom_role) that defines what the agent is allowed to do across the application
- for objects that support sharing (memberships) — for example projects — the agent must be granted access before it can read or act on them
- it can connect to connectors (external tools and services)

Any recurring or scheduled work the agent should do — periodic summaries, reminders, status checks, follow-ups, and similar — is expressed as a trigger, stored on the automations resource and filtered by agent_id.

Access to the agent itself is governed by memberships on the agent.

Two memberships are created automatically when an agent is created:
- one for the agent's manager (via the agent_manager dynamic group, with full access)
- one for the creator (person membership, read access)

Agents are activated or deactivated via the `activate` and `deactivate` actions rather than deletion.

companies.description:
Company represents a client organization or the user's own organization.
Client companies are the central hub for managing client relationships — they link to deals, budgets, projects, contacts, and invoices.

Each company can define default invoicing settings (subsidiary, invoice template, tax rate, payment terms) that auto-apply when creating new deals, budgets, or invoices for that client.
Companies support hierarchical structures via parent_company_id, tags for categorization, and custom fields for additional data.
Rate cards can be linked to companies to define client-specific pricing.
The organization's own company is used for internal (non-billable) projects and as the default rate card source.
Companies can be archived when no longer active.

The value key matches the singular of the list key (e.g. emails → `email`). At most one address may set `billing_address: true`

contracts.description:
Contract is the configuration record that drives a budget's recurrence — it links a template budget
to its auto-generated instances and stores the recurrence schedule and per-recurrence settings.
The actual budgets are individual records on the deals resource — recurrence applies only to production budgets, not sales deals.

"Contract" is the internal model name; user-facing references should use "recurring budget" instead.

Recurring budgets should be queried via the deals resource (with a contract relation) — not Contracts.
Contracts are used only to read or update the recurrence configuration of a specific contract.

Deleting a contract that has more than one linked budget is destructive — it detaches every budget in the
recurrence (clears the contract link, suffix, and end_date) and silently breaks historical recurrence.

Interval or schedule changes are not supported in place: switching interval, "resetting" the schedule, or
restarting with new settings requires a freshly created budget paired with a new contract.

deals.description:
Deal represents a potential or actual job with a client company.
Deals are a polymorphic resource with two subtypes (differentiated by stage_type):
- Sales Deals (budget=false) — track opportunities through pipeline stages with win probability for revenue forecasting. Time can be tracked for presales work but is not billable until the deal is won.
- Production Budgets (budget=true) — active jobs where work is delivered, tracked, and billed. Budgets can be client-facing (billable) or internal (non-billable).

Deals contain Services — line items that define deliverables with billing types (Fixed, Time and materials, Non billable, Percentage), pricing, quantity, and where time entries and expenses are tracked.
Services can be organized into Sections and can be moved between deals/budgets.
Deals can be linked to Projects for task management.
Financial tracking includes revenue, cost (labor + expenses), profit, and margin. Invoicing is only possible from budgets, not from sales deals directly.

Budgets can be recurring (retainer) — configured through Contracts, which auto-generate new budget occurrences at set intervals.
Recurring budget reference format: "Name (suffix)" — Name is the template name shared by every occurrence in the chain, suffix is the per-occurrence label. Both required.

Deals is a polymorphic resource with subtypes: sales deals and budgets.
Each subtype has a different default filter scope:
- sales deals: { stage_type: {eq: '1'}, stage_status: {eq: '1'} }
- budgets: { stage_type: {eq: '2'}, status: {eq: '1'} }
When users ask about "deals" without specifying a subtype, the default is sales deals.
Users typically refer to production budgets just as "budgets".

pages.description:
Page is a rich text document in a hierarchical structure. A page is either a root page (what users call a "Doc") or a child page nested under a parent within the same Doc.
- Root page (Doc): has no parent_page_id or root_page_id. Can be linked to a Project or standalone. Owns all sharing and access settings — child pages inherit them.
- Child page: must set both parent_page_id and root_page_id on creation. Nested arbitrarily deep.

Sharing is controlled at the Doc (root page) level via Memberships:
- Access levels: view, comment, edit, or full access. Can be granted to individuals or teams.
- Project docs are visible to project members by default; standalone docs are visible only to their creator.
- Docs can also be shared publicly via a read-only web link (public_access).

Pages support rich formatting (ProseMirror schema): tables, lists, checklists, banners, embedded files/images, and cover images.
Individual blocks (paragraphs, headings, lists, tables, banners, ...) have stable identifiers, enabling deep-links that scroll directly to a specific block or section inside a Doc.

people.description:
Person is the central resource in Productive — most other resources reference people as assignees, creators, approvers, or responsible parties.
People is a polymorphic resource with five subtypes:

1. Employees:
Full organization members with login access. Count as paid seats.
Can be assigned to tasks, track time, log expenses, be booked on services in the Resource Planner, and request time off.
Have cost rates (salaries) that determine hourly cost for profitability tracking, working capacity, and holiday calendar.
Assigned to teams, subsidiaries, and service types. Have a manager for org chart hierarchy.
Permissions are controlled via system or custom permission sets.

2. Contractors:
External collaborators with login access, employed by a different company. Count as paid seats.
Same capabilities as employees (tasks, time tracking, bookings, cost rates) but linked to an external company.
Overhead is typically disabled on their cost rates since they don't generate organizational overhead.

3. Clients:
External users invited to collaborate on specific projects. Free seats (no cost).
Client Staff: can view and manage tasks, comment, and collaborate on docs within shared projects.
Client Managers: additionally can view budgets and a client-facing subset of financial data (services, time entries, expenses) on budgets where client access is enabled.
Cannot access profitability data, cost rates, or internal projects. Custom client permissions can be created for tailored access.

4. Contacts:
CRM records without login access. Store contact details, notes, and linked emails.
Cannot collaborate in the app but can be converted to any user type (Employee, Contractor, or Client) at any time via the invite action.
Archived via archived_at (not deactivated_at which is for users).

5. Placeholders:
Named resource slots for capacity planning before a real person is hired or assigned.
Can have cost rates and be booked on services in the Resource Planner, but cannot be added to projects, assigned to tasks, or track time.
Confirmed placeholder bookings can be reassigned to a real person. Available on Professional (5) and Ultimate (10) plans.

People can be active or deactivated/archived.
Deactivating and offboarding employees and contractors is performed manually in Productive by someone with permission to deactivate and offboard them.
People can set custom status (emoji + text with expiration) that syncs to Slack and external calendars.

projects.description:
Project is a workspace where work is organized and tracked.
Two types: client (project_type=2) for billable client work, and internal (project_type=1) for non-billable overhead.

Projects contain:
- Folders and Task Lists for organizing tasks. Tasks follow the project's Workflow (configurable task statuses).
- Docs (Pages) for documentation, shared with project members by default.
- Budgets linked for financial tracking — client projects have billable budgets, internal projects only have non-billable budgets.
- Surveys (Forms) for collecting structured data from users, with automations that can create tasks from responses.

New projects have no navigation tabs by default and are unusable in the UI.
When creating a new project, navigation tabs must be created.

Tasks within a project can be viewed in List, Board, Table, Calendar, Timeline, or Gantt layouts.
Access is controlled via Memberships — project members, teams, and clients can be added with varying permissions.
Clients can collaborate on tasks in client projects. With the Client Manager permission and explicit budget access enabled, clients can also view a client-facing subset of financial data (services, time entries, expenses) on budgets they are invited to.
Internal projects cannot have clients added. Converting between client and internal is possible but resets billable data.
Projects can be archived when completed. Archived projects have restricted editing — only name, project manager, and custom field values can be updated. Other fields, memberships, folders, and task lists cannot be modified until the project is restored.
Deleting a project automatically deletes everything it contains.

proposals.description:
Proposal is a sales document that presents proposed work and pricing to a client for approval.
Proposals are created on sales deals — each proposal is a snapshot of the deal's scope, pricing, and contact data at the time of creation or last sync.

Lifecycle: draft → sent → accepted or declined.
- Draft: editable, can be regenerated to sync with deal changes. Uses a document type for styling and layout.
- Sent: shared via email or public link. Generating a public link automatically sets status to sent.
- Accepted: client accepted (and optionally e-signed) via the public link. Signed proposals are locked and cannot be edited.
- Declined: set by the user in Productive, or by the client via the public link. Disables the public link for signing.

services.description:
Service is a line item on a Deal or Budget representing a type of work to be delivered (e.g. Design, Development, Consulting).
Services are the foundation of financial tracking — they connect time tracking, resource scheduling, invoicing, and profitability analysis.

Each service is configured with:
- A billing type: Fixed (agreed price regardless of hours), Time and materials (billed per actual hours/expenses), Non billable (internal tracking only, no revenue), or Percentage (value computed as a percentage of other services in the section, no unit).
- A tracking unit: Hours, Days (person-days), or Pieces (discrete items/expenses). The unit determines what generates or assumes revenue. Percentage services have no unit.
- Tracking toggles: time tracking, expense tracking, and booking (resource scheduling) can each be enabled or disabled independently.

Revenue recognition depends on billing type and unit:
- Time and materials by hour/day: approved time entries and future bookings generate revenue.
- Time and materials by piece: only approved expenses generate revenue.
- Fixed by hour/day: service holds all revenue upfront; time entries and bookings assume (transfer) revenue from the service.
- Fixed by piece: only expenses assume revenue from the service.
- Non billable: never generates revenue, only costs.
- Percentage: revenue is recomputed as a fee on the section's other services (e.g. 10% management fee).

Services belong to a Section within their deal/budget and are categorized by a Service Type (e.g. Design, Development) for cross-project reporting.
Invoicing is done from budget services — deal services cannot be invoiced directly until the deal is won and work is transferred to a budget.
Services can be moved between deals/budgets while preserving all linked time entries, expenses, and bookings.

tasks.description:
Task represents a unit of work that can be assigned to a person. Tasks live in a Project, organized into Task Lists within Folders.

Task hierarchy:
- Tasks: standalone work items with an assignee, workflow status, dates, estimates, and tags.
- Subtasks: nested under a parent task (via parent_task_id). Cannot be moved independently — moving a parent moves its subtasks. Can be converted to standalone tasks and vice versa.
- Key tasks: key deliverables or checkpoints (type_id distinguishes tasks from key tasks). Previously called milestones.

Tasks progress through workflow statuses (e.g. To Do, In Progress, Done) defined by the project's Workflow. Statuses belong to three categories: not started, started, and closed.
Closing a parent task does not close its subtasks, and closing all subtasks does not close the parent.

Tasks can include: todo checklists, time estimates (initial_estimate, remaining_time), start/due dates, attachments, subscribers, and an activity feed with comments.
Time entries can be linked to tasks for granular tracking of what work was done against which budget service.
Bookings can be created directly from tasks when scheduling is enabled, linking resource planning to task-level work.
Tasks can be private (visible only to subscribers) or public (visible to all project members).
Dependencies between tasks define blocking, waiting, and linked relationships.
Tasks are ordered within their task list; subtasks are ordered within their parent task. New tasks are appended to the end of the task list on creation.

time_entries.description:
Time Entry records work done by a person against a service in a deal or budget.
Time entries are the primary source of labor cost and revenue data in Productive.

Financial impact:
- Cost: worked time (time field) × person's hourly cost rate from their salary record.
- Revenue: billable time (billable_time) × service price. Only applies if the service is billable and the entry is approved.
- Billable time defaults to worked time but can differ (e.g. internal overhead logged against a billable service).

Tracking methods: manual entry, timer (start/stop), or automatic (from bookings, created at midnight for scheduled work).
Entries can optionally be linked to a Task for granular tracking of what work was done.

Lifecycle:
- Submission: if timesheet submission is enabled, entries must be submitted before they enter the approval queue.
- Approval: if time approval is enabled on the budget/deal, entries go through approved/rejected workflow. Only approved entries are recognized — they count toward budget usage, revenue, and can be invoiced.
- Invoicing: once a service's time is included on a finalized invoice (via line items), the backend marks matching entries as invoiced (`invoiced = true`) and locks them.
- Financial lock: entries in a locked financial period cannot be modified.

A person must have a cost rate (salary) defined to track time.

allocations.description:
Allocation is a read-only view of planned time for people in the Resource Planner.
Unlike bookings (which can be created/updated/deleted), allocations are aggregated read-only records
used for reporting and visibility into how people's time is scheduled.
Service allocations represent time scheduled on a project service (billable work).
Event allocations represent time off (vacation, sick leave, remote work, etc).
Allocations are stored in the bookings table but exclude canceled, rejected, and deleted bookings.

approval_policies.description:
Approval Policy defines reusable rules for who must approve submissions before they are recognized and billable.
Policies are typed by what they govern:
- Event (type_id=1): absence/time-off requests — approvers review bookings for vacation, sick leave, remote work.
- Budget (type_id=2): time entries and expenses on budgets — controls whether tracked time and logged expenses require review before affecting revenue and profitability.
- Deal (type_id=3): time entries and expenses on deals — same as budget policies but for sales deals (Beta).

Each policy specifies approver roles (manager, budget/deal owner, project manager, or specific people) and approval mode:
- No approval needed: submissions are auto-approved.
- Any one of the listed approvers: single approval is sufficient.
- All approvers: every listed approver must approve; a single rejection declines the request.

Policies can be set as default (auto-assigned to new budgets/deals) or assigned in bulk.
A policy only takes effect if the corresponding organization-wide approval feature is enabled (time approval, expense approval, or absence approval).
A policy on its own enforces nothing — approval rules are attached through approval_workflows linked to it.
Policies can be archived when no longer needed.

Approval Policy Assignment links an approval policy to a target entity — a person, budget, or deal.
Each target can have at most one active assignment per policy type.

- target_type "person": governs absence/time-off approval for that person's leave requests.
- target_type "budget": governs time entry and expense approval on that budget.
- target_type "deal": governs time entry and expense approval on that deal.

Without an assignment, a policy has no effect on a specific entity.

approval_statuses.description:
Approval Status is a per-approver record tracking one person's approval decision on a booking (absence), time entry, or expense.
When a submission triggers an approval workflow, one Approval Status is created for each designated approver in the policy.

Each record contains:
- The target entity (booking, time_entry, or expense) and its target_type: booking (absence booking), time_entry (time entry), or expense (expense).
- The designated approver (who should review) and the actual_approver (who performed the action — may differ if someone else acts on their behalf).
- The linked approval_workflow (the instantiated workflow that generated this status).
- An optional note explaining the approval or rejection reason.

Approval statuses are system-managed — they are created automatically when submissions enter the approval flow and updated when approvers take action.
Only after all required approvers approve (based on the policy's mode) does the target entity become recognized, billable, and available for invoicing.

approval_workflows.description:
Instantiated approval configuration for a specific scope under an Approval Policy. The scope is selected by target_type_id:
- Absences (target_type_id=1): one workflow per absence category
- Time entries (target_type_id=2): time tracked on budgets/deals.
- Expenses (target_type_id=3): expenses logged on budgets/deals.

Each workflow defines two participant groups:
- Designated approvers: explicit people (via the approvers relationship) and/or dynamic slots (via dynamic_approver_ids) resolved per submission. approval_requirement_id controls how many of them must act before a submission is fulfilled.
- Subscribers: explicit people and/or dynamic slots (via dynamic_subscriber_ids) who receive notifications but are not required to act.

Workflows are created after the parent approval policy exists. A budget or deal policy covering both time and expenses needs one time-scoped and one expense-scoped workflow under the same policy.

attachments.description: Attachment is a file uploaded to a Task, Page (Doc), Comment, Expense, or Invoice — attaching the same file to multiple parents requires a separate record per parent. Attachments store documents, images, and other files related to work. The URL field provides a download link to access the file content.

Automatic invoicing rule is the schedule (the "when") for a recurring budget's auto-generated draft invoices.
It pairs with an invoice template, which configures the generated invoices; a recurring budget needs both for automatic invoicing to run, and has at most one of each.

automations.description:
Automation defines a rule that automatically triggers actions based on events or schedules.
Every rule has three parts: When (trigger), Check if (optional conditions), Then (actions).

Trigger types (type_id):
- Event (1): fires when a target object is created, updated, deleted, or commented on.
- Time (2): fires on a schedule (daily, weekly, monthly) at a specified time.

Target types (target_id): task (1), deal (2), budget (3), invoice (4), survey response (5), project (6), booking (7), expense (8), company (9), employee (10), slack message (11).

Available actions: send Slack message, send email, create task, create subtask, update field, add comment.
Conditions narrow when the rule fires (e.g., only if deal owner is a specific person, or task type matches a value).
Automations can be scoped to specific projects or applied across all projects (resolve_on_all_projects).
Each automation tracks monthly_runs and monthly_action_runs against the organization's action limit.
automations.routingSummary: rules triggering actions (e.g. task creation) on events or schedules

bank_accounts.description:
Bank Account holds the payment details an invoice is paid to — the "Pay To" section on the document.
Each bank account belongs to exactly one subsidiary, and only that subsidiary's accounts are available on its invoices.

The subsidiary's default bank account pre-fills new invoices and invoice templates; either can point at another account of the same subsidiary instead.
An account that is set as a subsidiary default cannot be archived, and its subsidiary cannot be changed.
Archived accounts stay on documents that already reference them but cannot be applied to new ones.
bank_accounts.routingSummary: subsidiary bank details invoices are paid to

name.description: Account holder name shown on the invoice

bank_accounts.queryHints: Users typically care about active bank accounts, unless they specify otherwise. The default filter scope for bank accounts should be: { status: {eq: '1'} }

bill_items.description:
Bill Item is a line entry on a Bill, linking a specific expense (from the purchase order) to a received quantity.
Each bill item records how many units of a particular expense have been received in this delivery.
The sum of bill item quantities across all bills for an expense determines how much has been received vs ordered.
bill_items.routingSummary: line items on a bill — links a PO expense to a received quantity

expense.description: Expense this bill item is for

bills.description:
Bill records the receipt of goods or services ordered through a Purchase Order.
Each bill belongs to exactly one purchase order and contains Bill Items that specify the received quantity per expense.

As bills are recorded, the parent purchase order's payment status updates automatically:
not received → partially received → fully received.
Bills include the vendor's invoice number, date, due date, and description for reconciliation.
Currency is inherited from the purchase order.
bills.routingSummary: receipts against a purchase order, tracking what a vendor delivered

purchaseOrder.description: Parent purchase order this bill is for

bookings.description:
Booking represents planned time for a person on specific dates in the Resource Planner — the core of resource scheduling in Productive.
A booking must have exactly one of service_id (work booking) or event_id (absence booking), never both.

Two booking types:
- Work bookings: schedule a person on a Service in a Budget or Deal. Affect availability, contribute to scheduled revenue (for billable services), and appear as time tracking suggestions. Can optionally be linked to a Task for task-level planning.
- Absence bookings: schedule time off or remote work on an Absence Category (Event). Time-off bookings reduce availability; remote work bookings do not. Deduct from the person's absence allowance balance. Can go through absence approval if enabled.

Time distribution methods:
- Hours per day: fixed hours each day of the booking period.
- Percentage: percentage of the person's daily capacity (e.g. 50% of an 8-hour day = 4 hours).
- Total hours: total hours spread evenly across the date range.
Hours given per week or longer are the total across the range, not a per-day amount.

Booking status:
- Confirmed (draft=false): firm booking that counts toward capacity and scheduled revenue.
- Tentative (draft=true): soft booking for potential work. Included in availability calculations but communicated as tentative. Can be toggled to confirmed later.

Bookings can be canceled (canceled_at set) rather than deleted, preserving history.
Automatic time tracking can be enabled per booking — confirmed bookings auto-generate time entries at midnight.
Bookings can be split, repeated (weekly/monthly), and duplicated. Multiple people can be booked on the same service simultaneously.
The overwrite action on absence bookings automatically splits overlapping work bookings to accommodate the absence period.

Report confirmed and tentative (draft) booking counts separately rather than as a single combined total.
When displaying bookings, always include total hours alongside the rate. How to derive total hours:
- Hours per day: count working days (Mon–Fri) in the date range, multiply by time/60. Show as e.g. "4h/day × 5 days = 20h total".
- Total hours: use total_time/60. Show as e.g. "20h total".
- Percentage: show percentage only (total hours cannot be calculated without capacity data).

Comments support rich text formatting and can include attachments.
Hidden comments are private notes visible only to the creator.

When creating a comment, provide exactly one parent relationship (task, deal, company, person, project, invoice, purchase order, or comment thread).
Mentions format: @[Person:ID:Name] — ID is the person record ID, Name is their display name. Both required.

custom_domains.description:
Custom Domain represents a Mailgun-verified sending domain configured at the organization level
and linked to one or more subsidiaries. The domain is the source of truth for which sender
addresses the API accepts on invoice email send.

verified_at is populated only after Mailgun DNS verification passes. Only verified domains
authorize sending.

Each domain may carry an optional dedicated sender (email_sender_address) and a flag
(allow_user_email) controlling whether individual users' personal emails can be used at the
domain. The send action accepts addresses that match the dedicated sender or, when the flag is
set, an authenticated user's personal email at the verified domain.

custom_field_options.description: Custom Field Option is a selectable choice for a single-select (dropdown) or multi-select custom field. Each option belongs to a specific custom field and has a display name, position for ordering, and optional color for visual distinction. Options can be archived when no longer needed — archived options remain on existing records but are hidden from new selections.

Custom Field adds user-defined data to resources like tasks, deals, budgets, projects, people, companies, invoices, expenses, bookings, and services.
Each field has a customizable_type that determines which resource it extends, and a data_type that determines the input format:
text, number, select (single dropdown), multiselect, date, person reference, or file attachment.

Select and multiselect fields have associated custom field options that define the available choices.
Fields are organized into custom field sections for visual grouping.
Fields can be archived when no longer needed.

deal_contacts.description:
Deal Contact is a junction record linking a person (contact) to a deal.
Deals can have multiple contacts, ordered by position. The contact at position 1 is the primary contact.
Positions are sequential (1, 2, 3, ...). The API auto-shifts positions on delete but not on create or update.
Setting a position on create or update does not shift other records — without a subsequent bulk update
of all deal_contacts on the deal, positions become non-sequential (duplicates or gaps).
deal_contacts.routingSummary: person-deal links — multiple contacts per deal with position ordering

deal_statuses.description:
Deal Status (Pipeline Stage) represents a named stage within a Pipeline that deals progress through.
Each deal status belongs to exactly one pipeline and has an ordered position within it.

Stage names are not unique across pipelines — an organization can have stages with the same name
in different pipelines (e.g. a "Lead" or "Lost" stage in each sales pipeline). Looking up a stage
by name alone may return multiple candidates.

Each status has a stage status that determines the deal outcome when moved to it:
- Open (status_id=1): deal is active and in progress.
- Won (status_id=2): deal was successfully closed. Probability defaults to 100%.
- Lost (status_id=3): deal was not successful. Probability defaults to 0%. Can require a lost reason (lost_reason_enabled).
- Delivered (status_id=4): budget work has been completed.

Per-stage configuration:
- Probability (0-100%): default win probability for revenue forecasting when a deal enters this stage.
- Tracking toggles: time tracking, expense tracking, and booking creation can be enabled/disabled per stage.
- The stage status cannot be changed after creation, as it would affect all existing deals in that status.

Supported item types include: deal, project, budget, invoice, task, service, dashboard, time_entry, purchase_order, page, booking, event, expense, template, survey.

document_styles.description:
Document Style is the visual layer of generated PDF documents — fonts, colors, header and footer treatment, and logo placement.
Document Types reference a style: the type decides what the document says, the style how it looks, so one style can serve many types.

document_types.description:
Document Type defines the template layout and settings for generating PDF documents.
Four document types: Invoice (also used for credit notes), Proposal (for deals and budgets), Budget Status, and Purchase Order.

Each document type controls:
- Content: which fields appear (totals, line item details, attachments, notes, footer), their order, and layout.
- Localization: language and date format for the document.
- Visual style: linked to a Document Style that defines fonts, colors, headers/footers, and logo placement.
- Default tax rates: up to two tax components (e.g. federal + state) that pre-fill on documents.
- Subsidiary: determines which legal entity's branding and details appear.

Document types can be set as defaults per subsidiary or per client company.
Selection priority for invoices: client company default → subsidiary default → alphabetically first active document type usable for invoices.
Document types can be archived when outdated.

which maps service type IDs to KPD code IDs for automatic KPD code assignment on Croatian

emails.description:
Email is a record synced from external email providers (Gmail, Outlook) or received via BCC forwarding.
Emails can be linked to contacts, deals, budgets, invoices, projects, and tasks for relationship tracking and communication history.

Emails are organized in threads and appear in the activity feed of linked items.
Read/unread status syncs bidirectionally with the email provider.
Emails can be auto-linked to deals based on contact matching, or manually linked by users.

Lifecycle: unresolved → resolved or dismissed. Mostly read-only — email content comes from external sources.
Emails can be marked as read or dismissed via actions.

Note: This resource represents emails linked to CRM records.
Gmail and Outlook inbox thread browsing and management (listing, searching, archiving,
moving) is handled by the email_threads resource.

entitlements.description:
Absence Allowance defines the time-off allowance for a person on a specific absence category (event) for a defined period.
Only applicable to absence categories with a limited limitation type (limited by days or hours).
Distinct from the read-only `allocations` resource, which aggregates scheduled time from bookings.

Each absence allowance tracks:
- Allocated: total days or hours allocated to the person (e.g. 21 vacation days). Can include half-day allocations (e.g. 4.5 days).
- Used: days/hours consumed through approved absence bookings (auto-calculated).
- Pending: days/hours in bookings awaiting approval (auto-calculated).
- Available balance: allocated - used - pending.

Absence allowances are scoped to a date range (start_date to end_date), typically a calendar year.
A person must have an absence allowance before they can request time off for that absence category.
Holidays (from the person's holiday calendar) are excluded from balance deductions — booking over a holiday does not reduce the balance.

endDate.description: End date of the allowance period

events.description:
Absence Category (Event) defines a type of time off or remote work that people can be booked on in the Resource Planner.
Configured by admins. Examples: Vacation, Sick Leave, Parental Leave, Remote Work.

Each category is configured with:
- Absence type: time off (person is away, reduces availability for project work) or remote work (person works remotely, does not affect availability).
- Compensation: paid (included in internal cost calculations) or unpaid.
- Limitation: limited by days, limited by hours, or unlimited. Limited categories require Absence Allowances to define each person's annual quota.

People are booked on absence categories via absence Bookings (bookings with event_id set).
Absence bookings can go through an approval workflow if absence approval is enabled for the organization.
Categories can sync status to Slack and external calendars when status sync is enabled.
Categories can be archived when no longer needed.

restore_event.description: Restore (unarchive) a previously archived absence category.

expense_line_items.description: A line item on an expense, with a name, quantity, and unit price. Individual line items are managed via bulk operations on this resource. The expense_line_items field on the parent expense replaces all line items on every write and cannot target individual ones.
expense_line_items.routingSummary: expense line items with name, quantity, and unit price

expenses.description:
Expense is a non-labor cost, optionally allocated to a Service in a Deal or Budget (e.g. travel, accommodation, software licenses, subcontractors, stock purchases).
An allocated expense is tracked on a service with tracking unit set to Piece and expense tracking enabled. Without a service the expense is unallocated.

Each expense has several independent statuses:
- Approval: unapproved → approved or rejected. Only approved expenses affect revenue and can be invoiced. Approval can be required via policies on budgets/deals.
- Payment: unpaid or paid (with pay_on due date and paid_on actual date).
- Invoicing: not invoiced → drafted → finalized. Billable expenses can be included on client invoices.
- Reimbursement: not reimbursable, requested, or reimbursed. Tracks whether the employee who incurred the expense gets paid back.

Revenue impact depends on the service's billing type:
- Time and materials by piece: approved expenses generate revenue (billable_amount × quantity).
- Fixed by piece: approved expenses assume (transfer) revenue from the service's fixed total.
- Non billable: expenses generate cost only, never revenue.

Expenses can be linked to Purchase Orders for vendor management and financial compliance.
Billable amount can differ from cost amount via a markup percentage.

Constraints:
- A purchase_order can only be linked to an expense with a single line item (or no line items).
- unit_price and quantity on a line item are immutable once the expense is paid.
- Line items are immutable on approved expenses.

approve_expense.name: approve_expense
approve_expense.description: Approve an expense. Fulfills the pending approvals on the expense's workflow on behalf of the calling user.

unapprove_expense.name: unapprove_expense
unapprove_expense.description: Remove approval from an expense, returning it to the pending state so it can be edited or re-approved. Resets the approvals on the expense's workflow.

filters.description:
View is a saved configuration of layout, columns, grouping, sorting, and filter parameters for a record collection.

Views serve two purposes, distinguished by view_type:
- View (view_type=1): a saved perspective on a list screen ("My open tasks", "Overdue budgets"). Scoped to a filterable_collection.
- Report (view_type=2): aggregated analytical view with charts and grouping; can be added to dashboards as widgets.

A view's filterable_type determines where it lives.
- filterable_type='project' with filterable_id=<project_id> makes the view a project tab. The tab renders as part of the project's secondary navigation.
- filterable_type unset makes the view global.

Views can be private (visible only to the creator) or shared:
- Project views are private or public (toggled via is_public)
- Non-project views can also be shared per-user via memberships, with "Can view" or "Full access" levels.

Reports can be organized into custom categories for easier navigation.
filters.routingSummary: saved views (filters/sorters/layout/groups) serving as project tabs, in-app views, reports or dashboard widgets

filterableType.description: Polymorphic parent type the view belongs to. "project" for project tabs; unset for a global view

filterableId.description: ID of the parent resource referenced by filterable_type

columns.description: Ordered, comma-separated kebab-case column ids visible in the view; order sets display order; valid ids are specific to the `filterable_collection`; for `view_type` "View" the collection's primary column is always first; omitting it from a write has no effect

sortBy.description: Kebab-case column id the records are sorted by. Prefix with "-" for descending

groupBy.description: Comma-separated kebab-case column ids the records are grouped by. Date columns take a `:<bucket>` suffix (e.g. `date:month`); buckets: day, week, month, quarter, year, fiscal_quarter, fiscal_year

folders.description:
Folder is a container for grouping Task Lists within a Project.
A project can have multiple folders to organize work into logical sections (e.g. sprints, phases, work streams, priorities).
Each folder contains one or more task lists, and each task list contains tasks.

Folders can be reordered within a project, moved to another project (with all tasks and task lists), duplicated, and archived.
Archiving a folder does not change the status of tasks inside it — tasks may still appear in reports unless separately closed.
Tasks within folders can be viewed in List, Board, Table, Calendar, Timeline, or Gantt layouts.
folders.routingSummary: collections of task lists within a project (e.g. sprints, phases)

placement.description: Ordering value of the folder within the project

folders.queryHints: Users typically care about active folders, unless they specify otherwise. The default filter scope for folders should be: { status: {eq: '1'} }

archive_folder.name: archive_folder
archive_folder.description: Archive the folder. Archiving a folder also archives all its active task lists. Archived folders are hidden from active views but can be restored. Tasks inside are not closed by archiving.

reposition_folder.name: reposition_folder
reposition_folder.description:
Reorders an existing folder relative to its siblings within the project.
The folder is placed directly above another folder by passing move_before_id,
directly below another by passing move_after_id, between two folders when both
are passed, or at the end of the list when neither is passed.
Prefer invoking only when the user explicitly asks for a different order —
listing items in a prompt is not by itself an ordering signal.

restore_folder.name: restore_folder
restore_folder.description: Restore (unarchive) a previously archived folder so it appears in active views again.

holiday_calendars.description:
Holiday Calendar defines a set of public/bank holidays for a specific country or region.
Configured by admins. Each organization can have multiple calendars for different regions or subsidiaries.

People are assigned to a holiday calendar through their cost rate (salary) records.
Holidays in the assigned calendar are treated as non-working days — they reduce the person's capacity and availability across Productive:
- Resource Planner: bookings over holidays don't count hours.
- Time tracking: holidays are marked as non-working; time can still be logged manually.
- Absence booking: holidays are excluded from time-off allowance deductions.
- Workload layout: capacity shows as zero on holidays.

When autogenerate_holidays is enabled, holidays are pre-filled and updated based on the selected country and state.
When disabled, holidays must be added manually. If a state is not selected, only nationwide holidays are included.
holiday_calendars.routingSummary: organization-configured holidays per country/region that affect availability and capacity

holidays.description:
Holiday is a specific non-working day within a Holiday Calendar (e.g. Christmas, New Year, Independence Day).
Each holiday has a name and date, and belongs to exactly one holiday calendar.

Holidays reduce availability and capacity to zero for that day for all people assigned to the parent calendar.
They are excluded from absence allowance calculations — booking time off over a holiday does not deduct from the person's absence allowance.

To find which holidays apply to a specific person, look up the holiday calendar assigned to their active salary (cost rate) and filter holidays by that calendar.

Holidays can be auto-generated by the parent calendar (based on country/state) or created manually.
If an auto-generated holiday is deleted, it will not reappear unless the calendar is recreated.
holidays.routingSummary: organization-configured non-working day within a holiday calendar

after.description: Filter holidays on or after this date

before.description: Filter holidays on or before this date

integrations.description: External service connected to the organization. Calendar integrations (Google Calendar, Outlook Calendar) sync events; email integrations (Gmail, Outlook Mail) power the inbox — realm_id holds the connected email address.
integrations.routingSummary: connected external services (Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook, Slack, Xero, etc.)

realmId.description: Account ID — email address for email integrations

calendars.description: List of calendars available from this integration

lastSyncedAt.description: When the integration last synced data

invoice_attributions.description:
Invoice Attribution is a junction record linking an Invoice to a Budget (deal with budget=true), specifying what portion of the invoice amount is attributed to that budget.

A single invoice can span multiple budgets — each attribution defines the amount allocated to one budget.
This enables:
- Split invoicing: one invoice covers work from several budgets for the same client.
- Budget invoicing tracking: the attributed amount feeds into the budget's "invoiced" and "pending_invoicing" calculations.

Optionally scoped to a date range (date_from, date_to) for time-based billing periods (e.g. monthly time-and-materials invoicing).
The currency is inherited from the invoice and is read-only on the attribution.
invoice_attributions.routingSummary: links between invoices and budgets defining the attributed amount

dateFrom.description: Start of the billing period for this attribution

dateTo.description: End of the billing period for this attribution

budget.description: Deal/budget this invoice amount is attributed to

invoices.description:
Invoice is a financial document a company issues to a client, with Line Items detailing the billed (or credited) work.

Polymorphic resource with two subtypes (differentiated by invoice_type):
- Regular Invoice (invoice_type=1) — bills the client; created from budgets.
- Credit Note (invoice_type=2) — reverses or adjusts a finalized regular invoice (its parent_invoice). The parent's line items lock for editing once a finalized credit note exists.

Invoice lifecycle: draft → finalized → sent → paid. Credit notes do not reach paid — they offset their parent at finalize.
- Draft: freely editable, no invoice number yet. Line items can be generated from uninvoiced time & expenses, total/remaining budget amount, or a percentage of total budget.
- Finalized: invoice number assigned, locked by default. Only users with edit-finalized permission can unlock. Currency is locked on the budget once the first invoice (even draft) exists.
- Sent: reached either by dispatching an email (sets sent_on as a side effect) or by recording sent_on directly. Payment reminders can be added on regular invoices. Cannot be edited unless marked as unsent first.
- Paid: fully paid (tracked via Payments). Partial payments are possible — amount_paid, amount_unpaid, and amount_written_off track the payment state.

Each invoice belongs to a client company and subsidiary (issuing legal entity).
Invoices are linked to one or more budgets via Invoice Attributions, which specify how much of the invoice amount is attributed to each budget.
Supports tax calculations per line item, discounts, purchase order numbers, multi-currency, tags, custom fields, and export to accounting tools.

Amount is the net figure (without tax). Amount with Tax is the gross figure.
Users typically interpret unqualified "amounts", "revenue", or "totals" as gross figures.

Issuance-to-payment duration has no pre-aggregated field; it can be derived from invoiced_on and paid_on at the invoice level.
The Paid In field on invoice_reports measures due-date-to-payment, not issuance-to-payment.
invoices.routingSummary: billing documents (invoices and credit notes), draft → finalized → sent → paid

invoiceTypeId.description: Whether this is a regular invoice or a credit note

sentOn.description: Date the invoice was sent to the client

paidOn.description: Date the invoice was fully paid. Never set on credit notes.

invoiceState.description: Filter-only; a record carries its state in finalized_on (null while draft)

sentStatus.description: Filter-only; a record carries its status in sent_on (null while unsent)

exported.description: Whether the invoice has been exported to an accounting system

credited.description: True on a regular invoice once a finalized credit note points to it; always false on credit notes.

paymentTerms.description: Number of days between invoice date and due date

payOnRelative.description: true ⇒ pay_on was set relative to invoiced_on (e.g. Net 30). pay_on remains an absolute date the caller sets explicitly (no auto-compute). UI keeps the offset stable when invoiced_on changes

footer.description: Footer text inherited from the document type at selection time

amountUnpaid.description: Remaining unpaid amount; zero on credit notes.

amountCredited.description: Net amount covered by finalized credit notes pointing to this invoice; zero on credit notes.

creationOptions.description: Line item generation settings (invoicing method, display format, grouping, date interval)

documentType.description: Only invoice-kind document types are valid

billTo.description: Billing recipient (name, country, address, VAT of the client)

billFrom.description: Billing sender (name, country, address, VAT of the issuing subsidiary)

parentInvoice.description: The finalized regular invoice this credit note reverses or adjusts; required on credit notes, null on regular invoices.

bankAccount.description: Bank account the invoice is paid to, from the invoice subsidiary's accounts. Locked once the invoice is sent

bankAccountDetails.description: Pay To details the document, the invoice email and the e-invoice render. Stored verbatim, so it is written together with bank_account, carrying that account's fields. Locked once the invoice is sent

attachment.description: File that replaces the generated PDF in the invoice email. The link is set on the attachment record, in its `invoice` relationship

invoiceAttributions.description: Attributions linking the invoice to deals/budgets (amount per budget)

query.description: Matches number, subject, company and project

invoices.queryHints:
Unqualified "invoices" means regular invoices; the default scope is { invoice_type: {eq: '1'} }. "Credit notes" means { invoice_type: {eq: '2'} }.
Outstanding, unpaid, overdue, paid, payment-status, billing volume, and AR questions stay on regular invoices; those concepts do not apply to credit notes.
The invoice_type filter is dropped only when the user explicitly asks for both subtypes combined, and the answer names that scope.

finalize_invoice.name: finalize_invoice
finalize_invoice.description: Finalize a draft invoice — assigns finalized_on, locks the invoice, and either auto-generates `number` (when subsidiary has invoice_number_format) or uses the provided one. Preconditions: document_type set and every line item has a tax_rate. Not reversible without admin permissions.

send_invoice.name: send_invoice
send_invoice.description: Dispatches the invoice as an email. Each call delivers a fresh message — repeated calls re-deliver. Recipients and sender are not resolved server-side; the caller composes `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `from`, `subject`, and `body`. `from` is optional. `sent_on` is set as a server-side side effect of the dispatch.

invoice_templates.description:
Invoice template is the per-recurring-budget configuration for auto-generated draft invoices — issuing details and line-item generation settings.
It pairs with an automatic invoicing rule, which defines the schedule (the "when"); a recurring budget needs both for automatic invoicing to run, and has at most one of each.

budget.description: Recurring budget the template applies to

documentType.description: Invoice document type applied to generated invoices

subsidiary.description: Issuing legal entity for generated invoices

issuer.description: Person issuing the invoice. Defaults to the current user on create

bankAccount.description: Bank account copied onto generated invoices, from the template subsidiary's accounts

bankAccountDetails.description: Pay To details copied onto generated invoices. Stored verbatim, so it is written together with bank_account, carrying that account's fields

note.description: Derived from the document type; copied onto generated invoices

invoiceCreationOptions.description: Line item generation settings — invoicing method, display format, grouping, percentage, date interval. Absent means generated invoices have no line items

subject.description: Derived from the budget name; copied onto generated invoices

companyId.description: Client company of the template's budget — exposed as a direct filter

job_roles.description:
Job Role is an organization-defined classification assigned to people, such as Senior Designer or Project Manager.
A person can have at most one job role. Job role is a filter, group, and sort dimension on people, people reports, and capacity reports.
A job role is distinct from a custom_role permission set and from the person's free-text title.
Job roles cannot be deleted, only archived. Archiving makes a role unavailable for new assignments
and requires no unassigning — people keep their assignment and it remains available for historical reporting.
job_roles.routingSummary: organization-defined people classifications, distinct from permission sets and free-text titles
job_roles.queryHints: Users typically care about active job roles, unless they specify otherwise. The default filter scope should be: { status: {eq: '1'} }

archive_job_role.name: archive_job_role
archive_job_role.description: Archives a job role so it is no longer available for new assignments.

restore_job_role.name: restore_job_role
restore_job_role.description: Restores a previously archived job role for new assignments.

kpd_codes.description:
KPD (Klasifikacija Proizvoda po Djelatnostima) codes are product classification codes
used in Croatian e-invoicing. Each code classifies a product or service for tax and
regulatory purposes. KPD codes (8-character) are specific product codes, while NKD codes
(shorter) are broader activity classifications. These codes are assigned to invoice line
items for e-invoice compliance.
kpd_codes.routingSummary: Croatian product classification codes for e-invoicing compliance

isKpd.description: True for KPD codes (8-char), false for NKD codes (shorter)

line_items.description:
Line Item is an individual charge entry on an Invoice.
Each line item has a description, quantity, unit (hour/day/piece), unit price, optional discount, and a tax rate.
Amounts (net, tax, total) are computed server-side from quantity × unit_price - discount + tax.

Line items can be generated in three ways:
- From uninvoiced time and expenses: pulls approved, uninvoiced time entries and expenses from the budget's services.
- From total/remaining budget amount: creates line items for the full or remaining budget value.
- From a percentage of the total budget: invoices a fraction of the budget.

Generating from a budget (any of the three methods above) is the standard way to add line items to an invoice; creating or editing individual rows by hand covers manual, ad-hoc adjustments, mirroring the UI.

Each line item links to either a service or an expense (not both) for traceability back to the budget.
Descriptions support rich text and dynamic fields (e.g. person name, task title, period) for flexible presentation.
Line items can be grouped by service, budget, project, or task on the invoice.
Currency is inherited from the parent invoice.
Tax rate must belong to the parent invoice's subsidiary; tax rates from other subsidiaries are rejected.
Changing the parent invoice's subsidiary clears tax_rate, tax_name, and tax_value on every line item; they stay without a tax rate until reassigned from the new subsidiary's tax rates.
Line item ordering on a single invoice is controlled via the position field, not the sort parameter; cross-invoice sort or grouping is the line_item_reports path.
Line items are editable only on draft invoices.
line_items.routingSummary: invoice lines with quantity, unit price, tax, and optional link to a service or expense

taxName.description: Name of the applied tax (derived from tax rate)

companyId.description: Company on the parent invoice — same target as the invoice.company relationship path, exposed as a direct filter on line items

creatorId.description: Person who created this line item (distinct from the invoice creator)

updaterId.description: Person who last updated this line item (distinct from the invoice updater)

invoice.description: Parent invoice this line item belongs to

service.description: Service (billing point) this line item was generated from

expense.description: Expense this line item was generated from

taxRate.description: Tax rate applied to this line item

kpdCode.description: KPD classification code for Croatian e-invoicing

lost_reasons.description:
Lost Reason is a configurable label explaining why a deal was lost (e.g. "Price too high", "Went with competitor", "Unrealistic timeline").
When a deal moves to a pipeline stage with lost_reason_enabled=true, selecting a lost reason becomes mandatory.
Organizations define their own set of lost reasons for sales reporting and win/loss analysis.
lost_reasons.routingSummary: labels explaining why a deal was lost

mcp_servers.description: Organization-defined MCP server definitions. Admins configure which MCP servers are available; users create connectors to connect to them.

memberships.description:
Sharing entry (internally called Membership) grants access on a target resource — project, doc (page), dashboard, view (filter), survey, agent, skill, meeting, deal, or artifact — to a subject.

Access can be granted to a person (membership_type=1), a dynamic group (membership_type=2), or a team (membership_type=3).

Each entry has one target, identified by the matching target relationship (skill, project, page, etc.). Agents are people in the data model, so an agent's id is a valid value for the person relationship; the agent relationship is the target-side identifier used when the target itself is an agent.

Available dynamic groups depend on target type:
- View (filter): employees (shareable view/report only)
- Page (doc): employees; plus project_members and project_manager when the doc is linked to a project
- Deal: employees, deal_owner, designated_approver, project_members, project_manager
- Dashboard: employees, users_that_can_manage_project; plus project_members and project_manager when the dashboard is linked to a project
- Agent: employees, agent_manager
- Artifact: employees
- Meeting: depends on linked target
memberships.routingSummary: sharing entries — grants of access on projects, docs, views, dashboards, surveys, deals, agents, skills, and meetings

accessTypeId.description: Available levels depend on target resource type. Project, Deal: [member]. View (filter), Dashboard, Survey, Skill, Meeting: [full, read]. Agent, Artifact: [read]. Pages (docs): [full, write, read, comment]. Pulse: [full, write, read, comment]

targetId.description: Filter only — pair with target_type. Use for dashboard, meeting, pulse (no dedicated relationship)

targetType.description: Target resource type (read-only). Wire values: Workspace=project, Page=doc, Dashboard, Filter=view, Quote=deal, Surveys::Survey=survey, Agents::Agent=agent, Skills::Skill=skill, Artifacts::Artifact=artifact, Meeting, Pulse. Pair with target_id only for dashboard/meeting/pulse; others use dedicated relationship

team.description: Team being shared with. Required when membership_type is team

agent.description: Identifies the agent as the target when sharing the agent itself
