undismiss_notification.description: Restore a dismissed notification back to the inbox.

organization_memberships.description: Organization Membership links a user to an organization, granting them access. Each membership connects a person (profile) and a user (login account) to a specific organization. A user can be a member of multiple organizations.
organization_memberships.routingSummary: links between users and organizations, granting access

organization_subscriptions.description: Organization Subscription holds the current pricing plan and product entitlements for an organization. Exposes which subscription features are available (switch on/off) or metered (with usage limits). Read-only — subscriptions are managed through billing.
organization_subscriptions.routingSummary: pricing plan and feature entitlements for an organization

organizations.description: Organization is the top-level account in Productive. It represents a company that uses Productive to manage its business operations. An organization owns all other data — projects, deals, people, invoices, etc. It defines global settings: currency, time zone, fiscal year, working hours, locale, and date/number formats. Organizations contain subsidiaries (legal entities), service types, workflows, pipelines, rate cards, tax rates, and custom fields.

fiscalYearStart.description: Date when the fiscal year starts

releaseChannel.description: Release channel for feature flags: stable, beta, or alpha

exchangeRateProviderId.description: Determines which currencies the organization can use

manDayMinutes.description: Minutes per man-day; used for time→man-day conversion in reports

numberFormatId.description: Number display format preference (e.g. decimal/thousand separators)

timeTrackingPolicyId.description: Default time tracking policy applied to new people

page_versions.description:
A page version is an entry in a doc's version history — a snapshot of a page
at one point in time, recording who made the edit (person), when (created_at), and the page it
belongs to. Each content edit creates a version; consecutive edits by the same person within a
short window merge into one.

Query it for any version-history question — a doc's edit timeline, who edited a page, which
pages a person edited, when a page last changed. Filter by person or page, sort by created_at.
The same page recurs across its versions, so collapse by page when you need distinct docs.
page_versions.routingSummary: version-history entries for a doc — who edited a page and when

name.description: Name of a manually saved version; empty for auto-saved edits

titleSnapshot.description: Page title at the time of this version

restoredFromVersionId.description: Set when this version is a restore marker — the version the page was restored to

payment_reminder_sequences.description:
Payment reminder sequence is a reusable template for payment reminders.
Each sequence holds a set of payment_reminder definitions that act as templates rather than scheduled emails.
One sequence per organization can carry the default flag (default_sequence).
Deleting a sequence cascades to its template reminders; invoice-level reminders previously cloned from those templates remain unaffected.
payment_reminder_sequences.routingSummary: reusable payment reminder templates that can be applied to invoices

defaultSequence.description: Whether this is the org's default sequence. Setting true unsets the previous default

payment_reminder_sequences.defaultSort: Sorted by name ascending by default

payment_reminders.description:
Payment reminder is a scheduled email sent to a client about an unpaid invoice.
Each reminder belongs to exactly one of: an invoice (an actual reminder) or a payment_reminder_sequence (a template).
Creating an invoice-level reminder requires the invoice to be sent (sent_on set) and to have a due date (pay_on set).
Update and delete are accepted only while sent_at and delivered_at are both blank.
payment_reminders.routingSummary: scheduled email reminders for unpaid invoices — sent relative to due date

to.description: Recipient email addresses. Required for invoice-level reminders, not for template reminders

scheduledOn.description: Account-timezone date derived from pay_on ± reminder_period (sign per before_due_date); must be future

failedAt.description: Rarely populated; bounce/rejection failures live on the associated Email record

invoice.description: Invoice this reminder is scheduled against (actual reminder)

paymentReminderSequence.description: Template sequence this reminder belongs to (template reminder)

payment_reminders.defaultSort: Sorted by scheduled_on ascending by default

payments.description:
Payment records money received against an invoice, or an amount written off as uncollectable.

Two types of payment records:
- Payment (paid_on set): actual money received from the client. Reduces the invoice's amount_unpaid.
- Write-off (written_off_on set): forgiven debt that won't be collected. Reduces amount_unpaid and increases amount_written_off on the invoice.

Exactly one of paid_on or written_off_on is set on a record; both together or neither is rejected.

A payment can only be recorded against a sent invoice; recording one on a draft or finalized-but-unsent invoice is rejected.

Multiple payments can be recorded against a single invoice for partial payments.
When total payments + write-offs equal the invoice amount_with_tax, the invoice status changes to "Paid".

Payments with an external_id were synced from accounting tools (Xero, QuickBooks, Exact, E-conomic, Sage, Fortnox); the source system is authoritative for those records.

Currency is inherited from the invoice.

Per-row payment activity (recent payments, payments from a client, payments on an invoice) is read via this resource.
payment_reports is the aggregate path — sums, counts, grouped totals — not the per-row listing path.
payments.routingSummary: money received or written off against invoices

writtenOffOn.description: Date the amount was written off

externalId.description: Identifier from external accounting system — present on synced payments

date.description: Effective date — paid_on for payments, written_off_on for write-offs

invoiceNumber.description: Invoice number on the parent invoice

query.description: Matches invoice number, company and project

pipelines.description:
Pipeline defines the stages (Deal Statuses) that Deals move through.
Two types: sales (pipeline_type=1) for tracking opportunities from lead to close, and production (pipeline_type=2) for managing budgets.

Organizations can have multiple pipelines for different product lines, customer segments, or sales teams.
The number of pipelines depends on the subscription plan (Essential: 1, Professional: 3, Ultimate: 5).

Each pipeline contains ordered Deal Statuses (stages) with:
- A stage status: open, won, or lost. Moving a deal to a won/lost stage triggers the corresponding deal outcome.
- Default probability (0-100%) for revenue forecasting (Ultimate plan). Won stages default to 100%, lost to 0%.
- Per-stage toggles for time tracking, expense tracking, and booking creation on deals in that stage.
- Optional mandatory lost reason requirement when a deal enters a lost stage.

Configured by admins in sales settings.
pipelines.routingSummary: deal stages — sales pipelines for opportunities or production pipelines for budgets

prices.description:
Price is a line item on a Rate Card that serves as a service template.
When adding services to a deal/budget from a rate card, prices pre-fill the service configuration.

Each price defines:
- Service type, name, and description (template for the service).
- Billing type (Fixed, Time and materials, Non billable; Percentage is not supported on rate cards) and tracking unit (hour, day, piece).
- Rate (price per unit), quantity, currency, discount, and markup.
- Tracking toggles: time tracking, expense tracking, booking tracking, and budget cap.
- Estimated hours for internal planning.

Prices belong to a Rate Card, which is either a company-wide default (linked to the organization's company) or a client-specific rate card (linked to a client company).
When both exist, client-specific prices appear alongside company defaults when working with that client's deals/budgets.
prices.routingSummary: rate card line items with billing type, rate, unit, and tracking defaults

quantity.description: Quantity of pieces, hours or days that service is budgeting for

timeTrackingEnabled.description: Whether time tracking will be enabled

expenseTrackingEnabled.description: Whether expense tracking will be enabled

bookingTrackingEnabled.description: Whether booking tracking will be enabled

budgetCapEnabled.description: Whether budget cap will be enabled

proposal_sections.description:
Proposal Section groups Proposal Services within a Proposal.
Sections are a snapshot of the deal's sections at the time of proposal creation or regeneration.
They organize proposal services into logical categories (e.g. by phase, department, or deliverable type).
Each section has a name, position, and optional editor configuration for rich text content.
Sections are read-only — changes require regenerating the proposal from the deal.
proposal_sections.routingSummary: groups of proposal services which mirrors a deal section

editorConfig.description: Rich text editor configuration for the section content

proposal_services.description:
Proposal Service is a line item within a Proposal, representing a specific type of work with its billing details.
Proposal services are synced from the deal's services when the proposal is created or regenerated — they are a snapshot, not a live reference.

Each proposal service captures: name, description, service type, billing type (Fixed/Time and materials/Non billable/Percentage), unit, quantity, price, discount, markup, and computed totals (budget_total, revenue, discount_amount, markup_amount).
Services are grouped into Proposal Sections that mirror the deal's sections.
The origin_service_id links back to the deal service it was copied from.
Most fields are read-only — changes to the deal's services require regenerating the proposal to update.
proposal_services.routingSummary: deal service snapshots in a proposal with billing type, quantity, price, and totals

quantity.description: Proposed quantity in pieces, hours, or days

discount.description: Discount percentage on the proposed service

markup.description: Markup percentage on the proposed service

initialServiceId.description: ID of the initial deal service

budgetTotal.description: Total budget of the proposed service

purchase_orders.description:
Purchase Order (PO) is a document sent to a vendor to order goods or services.
Each PO is tied to a single budget and cannot span multiple budgets. Available on the Ultimate plan.

PO lifecycle: draft → finalized → sent → received.
- Draft (status_id=1): expenses are created as draft line items against budget services (services must have unit=Piece with expense tracking enabled).
- Finalized (status_id=2): all linked expenses are also finalized, impacting the budget. A PO number is assigned. This cannot be reversed — finalized POs cannot be reverted to draft.
- Sent: marked as sent to the vendor (manually or via email). Sent POs cannot be edited — clear sent_on (set to null) to mark as unsent first.
- Received: tracked via Bills that record received quantities. Payment status updates automatically (not received → partially received → fully received).

Each expense line item on the PO is a separate Expense record linked to a service in the budget.
Expenses linked to a PO must have a single line item (or no line items).
Expenses can be unlinked from a PO (keeping them in the budget) or deleted (removing from both).
Deleting a PO deletes all linked items unless unlinked first.
Supports multi-currency, vendor management, document templates, and export to accounting tools.
purchase_orders.routingSummary: vendor procurement on a budget; line items become budget-service expenses

issuedOn.description: Date the purchase order was issued

sentOn.description: Date the purchase order was sent to the vendor

note.description: Internal notes on the purchase order

sentStatus.description: Whether the purchase order has been sent

vendor.description: Vendor company this purchase order is sent to

deal.description: Deal/budget this purchase order belongs to

creator.description: Person who created the purchase order

query.description: Matches number, subject, vendor and budget

rate_cards.description:
Rate Card is a reusable price list containing Prices (service templates) for Service Types.
Used when adding services to deals/budgets from a rate card to pre-fill service configuration.

Two scopes:
- Company rate card: linked to the organization's own company. Available for all client deals/budgets. Limited by plan (Professional: 10, Ultimate: 30).
- Client-specific rate card: linked to a client company. Shown only when working with that client. Unlimited count.

Rate cards can be archived when no longer needed — archived cards cannot be used for new deals/budgets but existing ones remain unchanged.
Rate cards can be bulk-updated via CSV export/import for price changes across many services at once.
rate_cards.routingSummary: price lists for services — company-wide or client-specific pricing

company.description: Client company; or org's company for default rate cards

restore_rate_card.name: restore_rate_card
restore_rate_card.description: Restore (unarchive) a previously archived rate card.

revenue_distributions.description:
Revenue distribution models how a deal's revenue is spread over time — one or more periods (date ranges), each holding an amount and a percentage share of the total.

The same records back two features:
- Sales deals: Projected Revenue Distribution — spreads projected revenue across time for forecasting. Stored amounts hold the share of the deal value; the deal's revenue_distribution_base controls whether probability scales the forecast. With an amount-method distribution the period amounts are entered directly and sum to the deal's projected revenue.
- Budgets: custom revenue recognition — defines when fixed-price service revenue is recognized, independent of tracked time.

The deal's revenue_distribution_type controls behavior: 'default' (system-managed), 'even' (single percentage-based split), 'custom' (user-defined periods).

Periods are seeded from the deal's date/end_date at creation but edited independently afterwards — they are not required to overlap the deal's own dates. Exception: retainer deals are locked to even distribution, one period per contract interval; changing one period's start_on shifts the sibling periods in place (existing records are updated, IDs do not change).

Writing rules:
- 'even'-type deals: periods take amount_percent.
- 'custom'-type deals: periods take amount_percent or amount, matching the deal's revenue_distribution_method.
- 'default'-type budgets reject manually created periods — switch the deal's revenue_distribution_type to 'custom' first.
- Composing a schedule on an existing deal: the seeded period(s) already exist — query the deal's distributions first, then update or delete the seeded ones instead of creating new periods alongside them.
- Closed budgets and locked financial months reject changes.
revenue_distributions.routingSummary: periods of a deal's revenue timeline — projected revenue spread on deals, revenue recognition on budgets

endOn.description: Must be on or after start_on

amountPercent.description: Share of the total distributable revenue assigned to this period (0-100). Periods are allowed to sum to less or more than 100 — do NOT normalize the sum across a deal's periods

amount.description: Absolute money share for this period in the deal currency. Writable only on custom-type deals with revenue_distribution_method=amount; otherwise derived from amount_percent

revenue_distributions.queryHints:
A deal's revenue timeline (projected revenue on sales deals, revenue recognition on budgets) starts at the earliest start_on across its distributions — query with a deal filter sorted by start_on ascending to inspect it.
Even distribution means a single record, except retainers: retainer deals are even-type but hold one record per contract interval. Custom deals hold user-defined periods. A start_on range filter matches a deal when any of its periods falls in the range, even when a different period is the earliest.

roles.description: Permission set (the roles API resource) defines a named group of permissions that controls what a person can do in the organization. Roles are assigned to users to grant or restrict access to features such as project management, invoicing, time tracking, and administration. Each role targets a specific user type (employee, contractor, or client). Resolved permissions show the final effective permissions after inheritance is applied. Permission sets are access control, not job classification — what a person does is described by their job role (the organization-defined job_roles resource, where enabled) or their free-text title.
roles.routingSummary: permission sets controlling what a person can do in the organization, distinct from organization-defined job roles

permissions.description: Backend REPLACES the entire permissions hash on PATCH (not merge). To change a single key without losing others, first load the role to read the current permissions, merge the change locally, then send the full hash on update

roles.queryHints: An unqualified request about "roles" or "user roles" is ambiguous: it may mean these permission sets or the organization-defined job roles (job_roles resource, where enabled). An answer that presents permission sets for such a request should also surface the other meaning — noting that job roles exist as a separate concept, or asking which one is meant.

salaries.description:
Salary (Cost Rate) defines a person's compensation and working capacity for a given period.
A person must have a cost rate to track time or be booked in the Resource Planner.

Each salary record defines:
- Compensation: a cost amount with a salary_type (hourly, weekly, biweekly, monthly, or annually) and currency.
- Hourly rate: auto-calculated from cost, working_hours, and salary_type. Used for cost calculations: Cost = worked hours × hourly rate.
- Working hours: array of hours per weekday (Mon–Sun). Defines the person's weekly capacity for availability calculations.
- Alternating hours: optional bi-weekly schedule (two different week patterns) for 9-day fortnights or 40/32-hour alternating weeks.
- Holiday calendar: assigned per salary period, determines which days are non-working for this person.
- Overhead: whether the person's time generates overhead cost for the organization (typically true for employees, false for contractors).

A person can have multiple salary records over time (e.g. raises, schedule changes). The active one is determined by date range (started_on/ended_on).
Hourly cost for fixed salary types is calculated using full-year capacity, not partial periods, to avoid inflated rates.
salaries.routingSummary: people cost rates: hourly cost, working capacity, overhead, holiday calendar

defaultSalary.description: Legacy flag — always false for new records. Active cost rate is determined by started_on/ended_on, not this flag

overhead.description: Does the salary generates overhead (cost) for the organization?

workingHours.description: Working hours per weekday (0-24). 7 values for one week, or 14 for alternating-hours mode

alternatingHours.description: Defines whether working hours capacity is alternating between two weeks

cost.description: Gross compensation amount per pay period (depends on salary_type)

hourlyRate.description: Hourly rate of the salary (auto-calculated from cost, working_hours and salary_type)

holidayCalendar.description: Holiday calendar assigned to this salary period, affects availability calculations

scenario_bookings.description:
ScenarioBooking represents planned time allocation for a person assigned to a scenario service (ScenarioItem).
It is the resource-planning counterpart of a regular Booking, but scoped to a Scenario instead of a live Budget.

Use scenario bookings to model how many hours each person will work on each scenario service within a given date range.
This enables accurate cost and revenue forecasting in what-if scenarios before committing changes to a deal.

Time allocation methods:
- Hours per day: fixed hours each working day of the booking period. Set the "time" field (minutes per day).
- Percentage: percentage of the person's daily capacity. Set the "percentage" field (0–100).
- Total hours: total hours spread evenly across the date range. Set the "total_time" field (minutes total).

Each booking must be created and updated individually — no bulk endpoints are available.

When the parent scenario is applied to the deal/budget, scenario bookings are converted into regular Resource Planner bookings.
scenario_bookings.routingSummary: planned time allocation for a person on a scenario service — the resource-planning layer of a what-if scenario

time.description: Minutes per day. Applies to hours-per-day bookings; not used with percentage or total-hours

percentage.description: Percentage of daily capacity (0–100). Applies to percentage bookings; not used with hours-per-day or total-hours

totalTime.description: Total minutes across the date range. Total-hours bookings only; read-only for other methods (auto-calculated)

totalWorkingDays.description: Number of working days in the booking date range

bookingMethod.description: How time is allocated: hours per day, percentage, or total hours

note.description: Optional note or comment on the booking

scenarioItem.description: The scenario item that this booking belongs to

person.description: Person for this booking (derived from scenario_item). Never pass on create/update — pass scenario_item instead

scenario_items.description:
ScenarioItem is a row under a ScenarioService within a Scenario. Each item is either a
person assignment or a named placeholder — person and name are mutually exclusive, and
exactly one must be set.

- Person assignment: set person; leave name unset. The platform derives the item name
from the person.
- Placeholder: set name; leave person unset. Used when the user has not chosen a
specific person, and always for piece-unit services (which never take a person).

Optional date range and rate overrides (price, cost, discount, markup) default to the
parent service. Supports bulk create, update, and delete.
scenario_items.routingSummary: rows on a scenario service — person assignments or named placeholders, with date range and rate

name.description: Name of a placeholder item. Required when person is unset; ignored when person is set (platform derives name from person)

startDate.description: Start date of this item's work on the service

endDate.description: End date of this item's work on the service

usedQuantity.description: Quantity consumed on the service by this item, in the service's unit (hours/days/pieces). For a person item it stands for the time booked across the item's scenario bookings, so it tracks the actual schedule rather than the service's planned quantity

discount.description: Discount percentage applied to this item's rate (0–100)

markup.description: Markup percentage applied to this item's rate

price.description: Billable rate override. Defaults to the scenario service rate

cost.description: Cost rate (amount per service unit; hourly for hour-unit, per-day for day-unit). Usually omit on create — platform auto-fills. For salary-derived value, use calculate_cost_from_salary

scenarioService.description: The scenario service this item belongs to

person.description: Person assigned. Omit to create a placeholder (set name instead). Always omit for piece-unit services

scenario.description: The scenario this item belongs to (via scenario service)

scenario_sections.description: ScenarioSection is a grouping of ScenarioServices within a Scenario, mirroring how Sections group Services within a Deal. Each scenario service belongs to exactly one scenario section.
scenario_sections.routingSummary: groups of scenario services, mirroring deal sections

scenario.description: The scenario this section belongs to

scenario_services.description: ScenarioService is a service line item within a Scenario, equivalent to a Service on a Deal. It defines the deliverable, pricing, and billing configuration for a what-if scenario. Scenario services are created when building out a scenario's service configuration.
scenario_services.routingSummary: service lines in a scenario with deliverable, pricing, and billing configuration

price.description: Per-unit rate. Required for fixed billing type. budget_total = price × quantity

budgetCapEnabled.description: Whether budget cap is enabled for this service

scenario.description: The scenario this service belongs to

scenarioSection.description: The scenario section this service belongs to

deal.description: The deal this scenario service is associated with

sections.description:
Section is an ordered grouping of Services within a Deal or Budget.
Sections organize services into logical categories (e.g. by phase, department, deliverable type, or "Expenses").
Each service belongs to exactly one section; every deal/budget has at least one section.

Sections are visible in the budget editor, time tracking (Client → Project → Budget → Section → Service hierarchy),
invoicing (line items can be grouped by section), and reports.
Sections can be duplicated along with all their services to speed up budget setup.
sections.routingSummary: service groupings within a deal/budget (e.g. by phase or deliverable type)

service_assignments.description:
Service Assignment is a junction record linking a person to a specific service within a deal/budget.
Used when the budget's tracking type is set to "Restricted by person" — only assigned people can track time and log expenses against that service.

If no one is assigned to a service, the restriction does not apply and everyone on the budget can track against it.
If the budget tracking type is not "Restricted by person", service assignments have no effect on tracking permissions.
Each assignment connects exactly one person to one service. A person can be assigned to multiple services, and a service can have multiple people assigned.
service_assignments.routingSummary: person-service links for time/expense tracking restrictions

service_type_assignments.description:
Service Type Assignment is a junction record linking a person to a service type, indicating which categories of work they perform (e.g. Design, Development).
Only one assignment per service type per person.

Used in two contexts:
- Tracking restriction: when a budget's tracking type is "Restricted by service type", only people assigned to the service's service type can track time and log expenses.
- Resource planning: filters people by their qualified service types when scheduling work in the Resource Planner.

Managed on the person's profile or in the service types settings.
service_type_assignments.routingSummary: person - service type links for tracking and resource planning restrictions

service_types.description:
Service Type categorizes the kinds of work an organization delivers (e.g. Design, Development, Project Management, Consulting).
Every service in a budget must have a service type assigned — it is mandatory.

Service types serve multiple purposes:
- Budget organization: categorize services for consistent structure across deals/budgets.
- Pricing: rate cards define prices per service type, standardizing billing rates.
- Tracking restrictions: when a budget uses "Restricted by service type", only people assigned to the service's type can track time.
- Profitability analysis: reports can analyze revenue, cost, and margin per service type across all budgets.
- Accounting sync: service types can be mapped to item/account codes in connected accounting tools (Xero, QuickBooks, etc.).

Service types can be merged (reassigning all services, assignments, and prices to the winner) or archived.
Initial service types are auto-generated based on the organization's industry during signup.
Configured by admins.
service_types.queryHints: Users typically care about active service types, unless they specify otherwise. The default filter scope should be: { status: {eq: '1'} }

archive_service_type.name: archive_service_type
archive_service_type.description: Archive the service type. Archived service types are hidden from active views but can be restored.

restore_service_type.name: restore_service_type
restore_service_type.description: Restore (unarchive) a previously archived service type so it can be used again on services.

slack_channels.description: Slack Channel represents a Slack channel connected to the organization via Slack integration. Read-only — channels are synced from Slack. Channels can be public or private, and active or archived. Used to configure Slack notifications for projects and tasks.
slack_channels.routingSummary: slack channels connected to the organization via integration

name.description: Channel name without the leading #. Matches the whole name, case-insensitively

query.description: Matches channel name as a case-insensitive substring; ignored when name is filtered

slack_channels.queryHints:
Channels with similar names are different channels; a near match is not the requested channel.
No match means the channel does not exist or is not visible to the integration.

slack_messages.description: Slack Message represents a message in a Slack channel or DM. Can be read from channel history or thread replies, and sent to channels or as direct messages to users.
slack_messages.routingSummary: readable and sendable slack messages (channels and DMs)

threadId.description: Slack thread parent message ID (ts format). Present on threaded messages; null for top-level

blocks.description: Slack Block Kit layout blocks (sections, images, actions, etc.) composing the message body

slack_users.description: Slack User represents an active workspace member in the connected Slack organization. Read-only — users are fetched from Slack. Bot accounts and deactivated users are automatically excluded.
slack_users.routingSummary: active workspace members in the connected Slack organization

name.description: Slack username (handle) without the @ prefix. Filters across name, display name, real name, and email via case-insensitive substring match

displayName.description: Display name from the user's Slack profile (may differ from real name/username)

realName.description: Full real name from the user's Slack profile

email.description: Email address from the user's Slack profile

title.description: Job title or role set in the user's Slack profile

avatarUrl.description: URL of the user's Slack profile avatar (72x72px)

timezone.description: IANA timezone identifier from the user's Slack settings (e.g. Europe/Zagreb)

statusText.description: Custom status text set by the user (e.g. "In a meeting")

statusEmoji.description: Custom status emoji set by the user (e.g. :calendar:)

subsidiaries.description:
Subsidiary represents a legal entity within an Organization (e.g. regional offices, divisions, brands).
Every organization has at least one subsidiary. Multiple subsidiaries are available on the Ultimate plan.

Subsidiaries hold the "Bill From" identity used on financial documents:
- Company name, tax ID, and address — appear on invoices, proposals, budgets, and purchase orders.
- Default bank account — populates the "Pay To" section on invoices and is used for e-invoicing.
- Default tax rate — pre-fills tax on invoices, deals, budgets, and expenses unless a client-specific rate is set.
- Logo — appears on exported PDFs.

Deals, budgets, invoices, purchase orders, expenses, and people (via cost rates) are each assigned to a subsidiary.
This enables per-entity financial reporting, multi-currency support, and correct tax handling across jurisdictions.
subsidiaries.routingSummary: legal entities within an organization with billing identity, tax rates, and bank details

archivedAt.description: When the subsidiary was archived (null if active)

defaultDocumentType.description: Default invoice document type for this subsidiary

defaultBankAccount.description: Bank account pre-filled as the pay-to section on invoices issued by this subsidiary

defaultTaxRate.description: Default tax rate applied to line items when invoicing from this subsidiary

customDomain.description: Mailgun-verified sender domain authorizing invoice email from this subsidiary

subsidiaries.queryHints: Always load active subsidiaries, unless asked otherwise.

survey_field_options.description: Form Field Option (internally typed as `survey_field_options`) is a selectable choice for a dropdown (select) or multi-select form field. Each option belongs to a specific form field and has a display name, position for ordering, and optional color for visual distinction in the form. Options are archived rather than deleted.
survey_field_options.routingSummary: selectable choices for a dropdown or multi-select form fields

archive_survey_field_option.name: archive_survey_field_option
archive_survey_field_option.description: Archive a form field option. The option is removed from selectable choices while responses that referenced it are preserved.

survey_fields.description:
Form Field (internally typed as `survey_fields`) defines a question or input within a form.
Each field has a data_type (text, number, date, select, multiselect, file, etc.), can be marked as required or optional, and belongs to a specific form.
Select and multiselect fields have associated form field options that define the available choices.
survey_fields.routingSummary: questions on a form (text, number, date, dropdown, multiselect, checkbox, file)

dataTypeId.description: Person is not a valid form-field type (unlike custom fields on tasks/deals, which do accept person)

global.description: true=reusable across forms in the org; false=scoped to parent form

sensitive.description: Sensitive data; submitted values masked for viewers without elevated access

showInAddEditViews.description: Renders the field in add/edit forms (still exists when false; just hidden)

aggregationTypeId.description: Aggregation method for number form fields in reports

formattingTypeId.description: Display formatting for number form fields

originField.description: Links a form field to a task custom field in the same project; on submission, the value is copied via the form's automation. Constraints: matching data_type; origin field must belong to the form's project; at most one form-field link per origin field per form; survey_field_options cannot be created on a form field with an origin_field (choices come from the origin field's custom_field_options)

archive_survey_field.name: archive_survey_field
archive_survey_field.description: Archive a form field. The field is hidden from new submissions while historical responses are preserved.

survey_responses.description:
Form Response (internally typed as `survey_responses`) is a single submission to a form.
Each response belongs to a form and stores the submitter's answers in the survey_fields map, keyed by survey_field.id.
The value shape for each entry depends on the parent field's data_type (see the data_type enum on survey_fields for per-type formats — e.g. multiselect returns an array of option ids, file returns attachment references).

Responses can be created authenticated (in-app) or unauthenticated (public submission via the form's public URL).

Responses trigger automations on create (creating tasks, sending Slack messages, sending emails, etc.) based on the parent form's automation configuration.
survey_responses.routingSummary: submission to a form, storing per-field answers

surveyFields.description: JSON map of survey field IDs to submitted values for this response

customFieldAttachments.description: Attachments uploaded for file-type fields in this response

surveys.description:
Form (internally typed as `surveys`) is a customizable form for collecting structured data within a project.
Forms are used for intake requests, client feedback, internal approvals, support tickets, and standardized data gathering.

Each form belongs to a project and contains configurable form fields.
Fields can be linked to existing custom fields to reuse definitions and prefill task custom fields on submission.

Edit access to a form is gated by the SURVEYS_MANAGE permission plus memberships on the form — these control who can change the form definition and read its responses.
Who is allowed to submit responses is a separate setting (submission_access).

Form submissions create survey_responses, which can trigger automations — creating tasks, sending Slack messages, or emails based on responses and conditions.
Responses are exportable to PDF, CSV, or XLS.
surveys.routingSummary: in-project data-collection forms (intake, feedback, approvals); submissions are form responses

publicUuid.description: Server-assigned; meaningful only when submission_access='public'. Identifies the form on the public URL

task_dependencies.description:
Task Dependency defines a directional relationship between two tasks within the same project.
Three dependency types:
- Blocking (dependency_type=1): the source task prevents the dependent task from starting.
- Waiting on (dependency_type=2): the source task cannot start until the dependent task completes.
- Linked (dependency_type=3): tasks are related but do not block each other.
Only Blocking dependencies are rendered in the Gantt, as an arrow.

Each dependency is mirrored by a reverse dependency on the other task (Blocking↔Waiting on, Linked↔Linked).
Creating, changing the type of, or deleting one propagates to its reverse automatically.
Dependencies are deleted when either task is moved to another project.
task_dependencies.routingSummary: directional relationship between two tasks in the same project — blocking, waiting on, or linked

dependentTask.description: Target task that depends on the source task

task_lists.description:
Task List is an ordered collection of tasks within a Folder in a Project.
Task Lists structure work into groups without imposing a predefined meaning — users define what lists represent in their context (e.g. sprints, phases, categories, priorities).
A task belongs to at most one task list; each task list belongs to exactly one folder.
Task lists are ordered within their folder; new task lists are appended to the end on creation.

Task lists can be archived when no longer active. Archiving a task list does not change the status of tasks inside it.
Archived task lists cannot receive new tasks.
When moving tasks between projects with different workflows, task statuses need to be mapped to the target project's workflow.
Task lists can be duplicated (with their tasks) within the same project or to another project.
task_lists.routingSummary: task groupings within a folder (e.g. sprints, phases)

query.description: Matches task list, folder and project name

task_lists.queryHints: Users typically care about active task lists, unless they specify otherwise. The default filter scope for task lists should be: { status: {eq: '1'} }

archive_task_list.name: archive_task_list
archive_task_list.description: Archive the task list. Archived task lists cannot receive new tasks but can be restored. Existing tasks inside are not modified.

reposition_task_list.name: reposition_task_list
reposition_task_list.description:
Reorders an existing task list relative to its siblings within the folder.
The task list is placed directly above another by passing move_before_id,
directly below another by passing move_after_id, between two when both are
passed, or at the end of the list when neither is passed.
Prefer invoking only when the user explicitly asks for a different order —
listing items in a prompt is not by itself an ordering signal.

restore_task_list.name: restore_task_list
restore_task_list.description: Restore (unarchive) a previously archived task list so it can receive new tasks again.

tax_rates.description:
Tax Rate defines a tax or VAT percentage applied to invoices and other financial documents.
Each tax rate belongs to exactly one subsidiary — only tax rates matching the issuing subsidiary are available on a document.

Tax rates can have up to two components (e.g. federal + state tax), each with a name and percentage value.
An "empty" tax rate (no components) can be created for tax-exempt line items to avoid displaying "0% tax".

Tax rates are applied per line item on invoices, with a default pre-filled from the subsidiary or client company.
Once a tax rate has been used on a finalized invoice, it cannot be edited — duplicate it and create a new one instead.
Tax rates can be archived when outdated; archived rates remain on existing documents but cannot be applied to new ones.
tax_rates.routingSummary: tax/vat percentages for subsidiaries — applied per line item on invoices

archivedAt.description: When the tax rate was archived (null if active)

tax_rates.queryHints: Users typically care about active tax rates, unless they specify otherwise. The default filter scope for tax rates should be: { status: {eq: '1'} }

archive_tax_rate.name: archive_tax_rate
archive_tax_rate.description: Archive the tax rate. Archived rates remain on existing documents but cannot be applied to new ones.

restore_tax_rate.name: restore_tax_rate
restore_tax_rate.description: Restore (unarchive) a previously archived tax rate so it can be applied to new documents again.

team_memberships.description:
Team Membership is a junction record linking a person to a team.
Create a membership to add a person to a team, delete it to remove them. A person can belong to multiple teams.
Team memberships enable team-based filtering, reporting, resource planning, and access sharing across projects, bookings, and time entries.

teams.description:
Team is a group of people who share skills, responsibilities, or work together on related projects (e.g., "Design", "Engineering", "People Ops").
A person can belong to multiple teams via team memberships.

Teams enable:
- Filtering and grouping across projects, bookings, time entries, and reports by team.
- Access sharing — team members can be granted shared access to projects and docs.
- Resource planning — view and manage team capacity in the Resource Planner.
- Reporting — team-based breakdowns of utilization, profitability, and workload.
teams.routingSummary: groups of people, used for reporting and access sharing

templates.description:
A Template is a reusable blueprint for creating Productive resources. A single template
targets exactly one kind of resource — a project, deal, budget, doc (page), task or report — given by
`target_type`. Its `target_id` points to the target resource holding the blueprint content.
Only the relationship matching `target_type` is populated — a project template has `project` set;
budget templates populate `deal`, since budgets are deals; a task template populates `task`;
report templates populate none; the rest are null.

Target resources are excluded from the default query scope (used in the standard lists and tables in UI); they are reachable only by id;
a template's content is edited by operating on its target resource.

Templates are created in one of two ways: blank from scratch (`target_attributes`) or by
copying an existing resource (`target_id`). Task templates are the exception — they
cannot be created from scratch, only by copying an existing task.

Deleting a template also deletes its target resource; restoring the template restores both.

name.description: Sets the name on both the template and its target resource

targetId.description: Points at the template's target resource, which holds the blueprint content

targetAttributes.description: Type-specific options whose allowed keys depend on `target_type`; required for project templates, optional otherwise

copyAttributes.description: Doc (page) templates only: booleans controlling what is carried over when creating from an existing doc

time_tracking_policies.description:
A time tracking policy defines the time-tracking rules and restrictions that apply to the people
assigned to it, governing how they log time. A policy can limit working schedules and restrict
overlapping time entries. Each person is assigned at most one policy.
For the day and absence limits, null means unlimited, 0 disables tracking, and a positive value
is the cap.

timers.description:
Timer tracks an active time tracking session for a person.
Each timer is linked to a time entry and records elapsed time in real time.

When stopped, the tracked duration is saved to the associated time entry's worked time.
A person can only have one active timer at a time — starting a new timer automatically stops the previous one.
If a budget has overrun limitations and the timer reaches the service limit mid-session, it is automatically shortened.
Timers are available in the web app and desktop widget.

timesheets.description:
Timesheet groups all time entries for a specific person on a specific date.
Acts as a daily aggregate container — one timesheet per person per day, containing all entries across different services and budgets.

Timesheets are the unit of submission in the approval workflow:
- Employees submit timesheets (by day or full week) to confirm their logged hours are ready for review.
- Once submitted, no new entries can be added for that day unless the timesheet is un-submitted.
- Managers can submit or un-submit timesheets on behalf of employees.
- A weekly timesheet is marked "Fully Submitted" only when all days (including weekends) are submitted.

After submission, individual time entries within the timesheet go through the approval flow (approved/rejected).
Rejected entries can be edited and are automatically resubmitted.

todos.description:
Todo is a checklist item within a Task or Deal. Todos break down work into smaller, trackable action items.
Each todo has a description, a position (order in the list), and can be assigned to a person and marked as closed (done).

Todos belong to exactly one parent — either a task or a deal, never both.
On tasks, todos serve as a lightweight checklist for sub-steps that don't warrant full subtasks.
On deals, todos help define next steps and sales actions to move opportunities through the pipeline.

workflow_statuses.description:
Workflow Status is a named stage in a task's lifecycle within a workflow (e.g., "To Do", "In Review", "Done").
Each status belongs to one of three fixed categories that determine task state:
- Not Started (category_id=1): task is pending, work has not begun.
- Started (category_id=2): task is in progress.
- Closed (category_id=3): task is complete or resolved.

Multiple custom statuses can exist within each category.

position.description: Position of the workflow status in the workflow

workflows.description:
Workflow defines the set of task statuses available in a project.
Each project is assigned one workflow, and different projects can use different workflows (e.g., a development workflow vs. a design workflow).

A workflow contains statuses organized into three fixed categories:
- Not Started: tasks that are pending, work has not begun.
- Started: tasks that are in progress.
- Closed: tasks that are complete or resolved.

Multiple custom statuses can be created within each category.
When switching a project's workflow, existing task statuses must be mapped to the new workflow's statuses.
Moving a status between categories (e.g., Started → Closed) immediately affects all tasks in that status across all projects using the workflow.
Workflows can be archived when no longer needed.
